hints: Focus on which functional groups are acidic enough to react with dilute NaOH(aq), carboxylic acids and phenols do, but simple alcohols do not.
Remember that excess $\text{LiAlH}_4$ reduces each $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ group to a primary alcohol $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, so work out what functional groups are left in J.
Compare tartaric acid, which still has $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ groups, with J, which has only alcohol $\text{OH}$ groups, to decide which will neutralise NaOH.
walkthrough:
**Spot the functional groups in tartaric acid**

Tartaric acid is $\text{HO}_2\text{CCH(OH)CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$. It has two carboxylic acid groups and two alcohol groups.

Think of it as a dicarboxylic acid plus a diol in one molecule.

**Find the structure of J after reduction**

$\text{LiAlH}_4$ is a strong reducing agent. It reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols:
$$\text{RCO}_2\text{H} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$$
With excess, both $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ ends are reduced, so J is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$, a tetraol with only alcohol $\text{OH}$ groups.

**Test each compound with NaOH(aq)**

Carboxylic acids are acidic enough to be neutralised:
$$\text{RCO}_2\text{H} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{RCO}_2\text{Na} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So tartaric acid reacts. Alcohols are very weak acids and do not react with aqueous NaOH, so J with only $\text{OH}$ groups does not react. Therefore only tartaric acid reacts.

options.A: Incorrect. This assumes alcohol OH groups also react with NaOH(aq). Alcohols like those in J are far too weakly acidic to react with NaOH, only the carboxylic acid groups in tartaric acid do.
options.B: Correct. Tartaric acid contains $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ groups which are neutralised by NaOH. J is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$ and contains only alcohol groups, which do not react with NaOH(aq).
options.C: Incorrect and reversed. It suggests the tetraol J reacts but the diacid does not. In fact carboxylic acids react readily with NaOH, while simple alcohols do not.
options.D: Incorrect. This misses the acid-base reaction of carboxylic acids. Tartaric acid definitely reacts with NaOH to form the sodium salt plus water, even though J does not.
